items.followUp: Why does the heart’s apex point towards the left side of the chest?

rubric.why: Identifies the heart’s position between the lungs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the heart lies between the lungs.

rubric.why: States why the heart is usually felt on the left side.
rubric.description: Heart lies mostly to the left
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that about two-thirds of the heart lies to the left of the midline.

modelAnswer: The heart lies between the lungs in the chest cavity.
About two-thirds of the heart lies to the left of the midline, so it is usually felt on the left side.

items.followUp: What is one role of a biologist working in agriculture?

rubric.why: Describes the application of biology to human health.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing how biology is used to diagnose, prevent or treat disease.

rubric.why: Describes how biology helps improve crops or crop production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a biology-related role in crop improvement or food-crop production.

rubric.why: Describes a biology-related role in fisheries.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing fish study, breeding, production or conservation.

rubric.why: Describes the application of biology to the care or breeding of livestock.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing livestock breeding, feeding or care.

rubric.why: Describes the biological management or conservation of forests.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing forest management or conservation of forest resources.

modelAnswer: 1. Medicine: Doctors and medical researchers use biology to understand the human body and diagnose, prevent and treat diseases.
2. Agriculture: Biologists help improve crop varieties and increase the production of food crops.
3. Fisheries: Fisheries biologists study fish and help with fish breeding, production and conservation.
4. Animal husbandry: Biologists apply their knowledge to the breeding, feeding and care of livestock.
5. Forestry: Forestry specialists use biology to manage forests and conserve forest resources and wildlife.

items.followUp: Explain how an enzyme acts on its substrate and is available for another reaction.

rubric.why: Gives the defining role of an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining an enzyme as a biological catalyst that speeds up a chemical reaction.

rubric.why: Explains that the substrate binds at the enzyme’s specific site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate binds to the enzyme’s active site.

rubric.why: Names the intermediate formed when the substrate binds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying formation of an enzyme-substrate complex.

rubric.why: Explains that the bound substrate is converted and products are released.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the substrate is converted into products, which leave the active site.

rubric.why: States that the enzyme is not consumed and can catalyse another reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the enzyme remains unchanged and can be used again.

modelAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst, usually a protein, that speeds up a chemical reaction by lowering its activation energy.
A substrate with a shape complementary to the enzyme binds to its specific active site.
The enzyme converts the substrate into product or products, which then leave the active site.
The enzyme remains unchanged and can be used again.
